utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to greet all and everyone. This is number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Mr. Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are Tuesday, the 16th of May, 2006. I would like to greet all and everyone present in the courtroom. There is a new person on the Prosecution side. Could you please introduce this attorney, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Pieter Kruger is with us this morning, and we also have a new case manager, Ms. Kim Fischer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There's nothing new on the side of the Defence. We're going to gain some time. After requests that came in to adduce some documents, Mr. Karnavas, I think a mistake was made. I give you the floor so that you could give us the number of the exhibits again. I think a correction needs to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I believe it's 1D 00417. That was an article from -- I think from a newspaper with the American ambassador, Hubert Okun. And there's 1D 00418, which was the European Community Conference, the draft convention. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... exhibits which were tendered on the 11th of May should be 1D 00417 and 1D 00418, and not respectively, which was admitted at the time of the 11th of May, 1D 00416, and 1D 00417. So I repeat for the record, sorry if it's not clear: The two exhibits admitted are 417, and 418. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. We shall bring in the next witness. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, also we would ask that the two videos that were shown yesterday be admitted. Those were 7437 and 1015.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. President, I renew my objection based on Rule 89(D) to exclude the evidence on the basis that it's more prejudicial than probative. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, for the record, if my colleague can indicate whether that objection is to both videotapes or just one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just to the one. I was very clear: As far as the interview of my client Dr. Prlic, absolutely no objection to that. It's the other one, the montage, the one that was the result-oriented video that was produced by the young lady. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges will confer, and we'll let you know what we decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I would just like to check that you can hear me properly in your own language. I would like to check that you understand the translation. If you do, please let me know and tell me that you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kaplan, you have been called by the Prosecution to testify. Before asking you to read the solemn declaration, I would like you to give us your name - first name, surname - and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Fata Kaplan. I was born in 1949. I was born in a place near Mostar and now I live in a place near Stolac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mrs. Kaplan. What is your occupation or do you not have one at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a homemaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You already testified before this Tribunal, or is it the first time you've come to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before a Tribunal in your country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before which Tribunal, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A court in Mostar. I just know that it's in Mostar. It's in our country, in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you read the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank you. You may sit down. Mrs. Kaplan, in a few minutes you're going to be asked to answer a number of questions that will be put to you by the representative of the Prosecution who is sitting to your right. I'm sure you've met him before. The Prosecution told me yesterday that they will need approximately two hours to put these questions to you. Once these questions have been put to you, the Defence counsel, who are sitting to your left -- there are a great many of them, but there are only six Defence counsels -- will put questions to you within the same time frame. In our legal jargon, this is what we call the cross-examination. You will come to realise that the questions that are put to you by the Defence team are very different from the questions that have been put to you by the Prosecution. If at any point in time this is a problem for you, please let me know. We will try and sort out the problem for you. As this kind of hearing can be tiring for the witness, we will have a break every hour and a half. So we will have a break in an hour and a quarter. We will stop around 12 -- twenty minutes past twelve for an hour and a half so that you can have a bite to eat, and the hearing will resume in the afternoon again. By and large, this is how this hearing is going to unfold today. I remind you that you have read out the solemn declaration and that you have sworn to tell the truth, which means there will be no false testimony. I think it's Mr. Mundis who is going to put the questions to you, so I shall now give him the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps if the usher could assist us by just moving the ELMO, because it's blocking my line of sight with the witness. I would be grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you tell the Trial Chamber a little bit about your personal, your family life.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I live in a village and I work our land. I have three children, and we know what happened to one of my children. We work. We are farmers. We don't do anything else, nobody's employed anywhere else. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what -- what village do you live in?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I live in a village called Pjesivac Greda, near Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Kaplan, how long have you lived in Pjesivac Greda, near Stolac?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I've lived there for 35 years now. I came to that village when I got married and have lived there since.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mrs. Kaplan, where Pjesivac Greda is located.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Pjesivac Greda is between -- is located between Stolac and Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is this location on or part of the Dubrava plateau?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's precisely where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you tell us a little bit about life in Pjesivac Greda in the 1980s and up to about 1990.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: To describe, what should I describe? This is just an ordinary village. You know what a village is like. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who lived in the village?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Bosniaks, Muslims, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what were the relations like between the Muslims and Croats in the village in the 1980s and up to about 1990?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Let me tell you openly: They were very good. We lived together, worked together, did everything together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, ma'am, did Pjesivac Greda, was it -- did it consist of various hamlets?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, quite a lot. There is the upper portion, and then there is Pjesivac Kula, and our hamlet is called Pjesivac Greda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And these various hamlets, were they multi-ethnic or did only one ethnicity live in each of the hamlets?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: There was one Croatian hamlet and then one Muslim hamlet, and this is how they were. There were some Serbs, but they were a minority, there were not many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you tell us how the situation in Pjesivac Greda changed in the early 1990s.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: It changed. It changed for the worse. They went to one side, and they were separate from us, and we were separate from them, and what was to be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, what exactly do you mean when you say, "They went to one side and they were separate from us and we were separate from them"? Can you elaborate on that?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Before the war, everything was great. We lived together, worked together, did everything together. But later on, after the war broke out, they just did their own business, and they were better informed about things, and we knew nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who is the "they" that you are referring to? What do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, do you remember when the war first started in and around Pjesivac Greda?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: What happened, they started shooting on one side. They started fighting and looting things from our homes, taking us to prisons and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mrs. Kaplan, about your children. You told us earlier you had three children. Can you tell us the gender and ages of your children.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I have a son born in 1971. My other son was born in 1977. I also have a daughter born in 1969, and then I had another daughter, and I came here to testify about her and how she was killed. She was my fourth child.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mrs. Kaplan, when either of your sons joined a military force?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. My oldest son joined the HVO once the Serbs withdrew from the plateau. This is when they joined, and they were together at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, Mrs. Kaplan, at the time your son, your older son, joined the HVO, who the HVO was fighting against, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When did the fighting between the HVO and the Serbs begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, ma'am. The year may be mischaracterised in the transcript. Can you tell us what year the fighting between the HVO and the Serbs began?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: In 71st or in 77nd, and then in 1973 -- I'm sorry, 1983. I made a mistake. It was in 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ma'am, are you sure it wasn't in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's okay. Let me ask you, if you remember, approximately how long did the fighting in and around your village between the Serbs and the HVO, how long did that fighting last for?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, not that long. They didn't fight for that long. Half a year. I'm not sure it was a full year. They simply stood guard, they went to the line, but there wasn't much fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, ma'am, how long did your oldest son who was fighting with the HVO against the Serbs, how long did he remain in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: He was there for about seven or eight months, and then he was wounded and hospitalised in Split and didn't go to the front any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After the fighting between the HVO and the Serbs was over, did peace return to the Dubrava plateau?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, for about half a year or a year or thereabouts, and not after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened after that year -- half a year or year of peace?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They simply went together and worked until nowadays when they started splitting again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when did they start splitting again, as you've put it?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: That was in '92nd or '93rd, when they started separating men from women, children, and the elderly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness may have said the month of July, but the interpreters are not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know the approximate time of year when this separations began -- these separations began that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: That was in 1993, on the 7th of July. No, I'm sorry, on the 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, on the 2nd of July, 1993, approximately how many people were living with you in your home?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, there were 13 families, and living with me were about 14 people in my own house, but there were 13 families in the hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the 14 people that were living in your house, who were these people?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. They were two families, but we lived together. Two brothers and their families, before the war. And they were the families, the two families of those two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And who were these two brothers?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Hamzo Kaplan and Salko Kaplan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Kaplan, who is Hamzo Kaplan?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: That's my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say, then, that on the 2nd of July, 1993, you -- you and your husband and your children, and your husband's brother and his family were all living in your house?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mrs. Kaplan, what happened on the 2nd of July, 1993, in Pjesivac Greda.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I'll explain that to you. In the morning at around 7.00, early in the morning, some soldiers came by. There were a lot of them, and they started gathering up the men. And they said, "You're not going to stay here long." There were some soldiers above the village and other soldiers in the village, which meant that nobody could escape. Then they rounded up the people that they had collected, and took them off to the camps by truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you a couple of follow-up questions. When you say, Mrs. Kaplan --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say, Mrs. Kaplan, some soldiers came by, do you know what those soldiers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The soldiers were wearing camouflage uniforms, with caps on their heads and insignia. I can't remember what the insignia were like. We had to flee. But I just know that they were wearing camouflage uniforms and had caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, ma'am, from what army these soldiers came?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Later on I learnt from our people that there were some of ours, the Stolac municipality and Capljina municipality, and there were some people from Croatia who joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, at this point in time, that is July 2nd, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- how many of the men living in your house were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, there was my son and my brother-in-law's son - he was in the HVO too - and my husband was the Territorial Defence. He would go to do this civilian duty, dig trenches, whatever they needed, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us a few moments ago, as reflected on page 10, lines 21 through 23, "they rounded up the people they collected and took them off to the camps by truck." My first question, Mrs. Kaplan, is --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- who -- who rounded -- who rounded up the people?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The HVO army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Kaplan, who were the people that were rounded up? Who was rounded up?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They were my relatives, the Kaplans. Whoever happened to be there. The Bosniaks, and two or three people from the village. They arrested them all, captured them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say they captured them all, can you tell us, Mrs. Kaplan, did they take men, women, children, just the men, just the women, just the children? Who did they take when you say --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Just the men. From my village they took -- do you need the names of the people they took?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you can remember any of the names of who they took on that day.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Do you want the name and surname or their parents' names as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, whatever you can remember would be helpful to us this morning.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Ismet Kaplan, Mujo's son. Samir Kaplan, Hasan's son. Camil Kaplan, Omer's son. Ale Kaplan, Osman's son. Murat Kaplan, Salko's son. And Hamzo Kaplan, my husband, he was taken away from the hill, from up on the hill. And those were all the Kaplan family members who were taken away in just one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened to these people that were taken away on the 2nd of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They were taken down there to the neighbouring area and then to the camp at Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long -- to the best of your recollection, how long did these people remain at the camp at Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Some stayed two months, others three months, and some others were there for nine months. They were there the longest, until the last man left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mrs. Kaplan, among the people that you mentioned, I didn't see your brother-in-law Salko Kaplan. Was he taken away; and if not, why not?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They didn't take him away that day, but they did later on. Not on the 2nd of July. He wasn't taken on the 2nd of July. He was taken away later on, on the 13th of July, and I'll tell you why that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let's move, then, Mrs. Kaplan, to the 13th of July. Can you tell us what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: It was terrible, but I'll do my best to tell you. On the 13th of July, at around 2.00 in the afternoon, I was in the house, and Salko, my brother-in-law, was there with his wife, my sister-in-law, and a small child, five years old. We were downstairs on the ground floor, and I heard something, and I said, "What's that that we can hear?" And they said, "Go outside and have a look." And I saw a lot of soldiers outside, a lot of people gathered there, women, children, and they were moving towards our house. I just went inside, into our house, and said, "Oh, there are lots of women and children and soldiers," and my brother-in-law said never mind. Two minutes later, one of these came into the house and said, "Get out." We obeyed and went outside, and he asked us whether there was anybody on the floor above. We said, "Go and check, we don't know." We didn't actually know. And when my daughter heard a lot of noise, that he was shouting at us, she went out onto the staircase and moved towards us, and my sister-in-law said, "Come on, get your clothes on and we're going to leave." And she said, "Where are we going?" Sanida said. And she said, "You've taken all our menfolk, where are you going to take us?" So that was the last time she spoke because there was a burst of gunfire and they shot her. And that's the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, how old was Sanida on this day, the 13th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: She was almost 18. Ten days to go before her 18th birthday. Her birthday was on the 24th of July, and she would have been 18. Thirteen days to her 18th birthday. You can check that out for yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the registrar, I would ask that the photograph marked 9067 be displayed for the witness. It's -- this is in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see that photograph, Mrs. Kaplan, on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. That's my daughter. I recognise her, yes. It's a terrible wound for me, but I have to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you tell us what happened to you after this incident where your daughter Sanida was killed?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I was standing -- well, I said to the soldier to let me stay there and look at my daughter, and he said, "No, you can't." And then we went out to the yard, to the entrance, and I just saw her lying there, dead, in a pool of blood. And then I joined the other people, the people -- the Bosniaks who were making us go, and we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, you just told us that the Bosniaks were making you go. Which Bosniaks were these?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, no. We went with the Bosniaks, but the army, the soldiers, made us go. They made the Bosniaks go because the Bosniaks were Muslims, and they made us go out of the village. You can check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Mrs. Kaplan, if you know, when you say the army, the soldiers, what army or soldiers were these?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: From the HVO. The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that three photographs be shown to the witness. These are not in e-court. We do have hard copies of these photos. These are 9554, 9555, and 9556. Let's start with 9556, please, the bottom one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Kaplan, you should see on the screen in front of you or on the machine to your right a photograph. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what you see in this photograph 9556.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I see a house. It's our house. And I can see everything around it. Can I point with my hand to show you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you -- if you look onto the right where you'll see the actual photograph, you can point on the photograph that's on the machine next to you.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: This is the house, and this here --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could I just --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: And this is the yard. That's the gate, and that's where we went in. That's the entrance. And she was coming down from this part of the house, down here, and reached this door here, and that's where they killed her. She lay dead between the window and the door at this spot. That's where she remained. That's how it was. You can see everything here. I can explain it to you. I know very well that that's my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just -- Mrs. Kaplan, just for the record, if you could please take that red marker, the thin red marker that you were pointing with, can you please place an X on the side of your house. Just draw an X, an X, on the house. Right on the picture. You can put it right on the picture, on the house.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: On the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Can you zoom in, please, so the picture's bigger. A small X or a large X?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think that's fine. We can make out the X. Now, Mrs. Kaplan, you also -- you also pointed to a few other things in the photograph. Can you do that again for us, and stop at each point when you point to something.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: This is the house. This is the yard. It's inside, it's the fence. But this is the ground floor. This is the first floor. You can see that. These are the steps, and I have a small house that way. But these are the steps. This is the gate leading into the yard. These are the steps that my daughter came down. She didn't get further than this spot here, and that's where she was shot. I'll show you everything in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. Kaplan, just again, we have to make some markings on the photograph. Can you circle the stairs that you told us Sanida came down. Can you circle the staircase.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: There you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Maybe -- maybe we need to take the thicker marker. It's a bit difficult to see. Ah, okay.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. We do have -- Mrs. Kaplan, we have a couple of other photographs I'd like to show you, but could you please put your initials and today's date on the side of that picture, perhaps on the white area.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps today's date, 16 May, 2006.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mrs. Kaplan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could now have 9555 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, do you recognise the photograph that's been marked P 955?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I know it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What do you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I can see the stairs, I can see the fence, railings, the window, the door, the little table. That's what it looks like now. The flowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, again, Mrs. Kaplan, could you take the thick marker and circle the stairs.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the location on this photograph where you were standing at the time your daughter Sanida was killed?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Here. Do you wanted me to place a mark there of some kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you could make an X.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I was standing here, and the people who were with me - that is to say my brother-in-law. She came down this way, and she reached the door here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say, "She came down this way, and she reached the door here," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: My daughter Sanida, the one who was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mrs. Kaplan, where was Sanida at the time she was killed?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: She was standing up here, up on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then where did she go?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: She came down these stairs, and my sister-in-law said, "Sanida, let's go." And she said, "Where are we going?" I said all this a moment ago. I'm am repeating what I said. She said, "Where are we going?" And my sister-in-law said, "We're going," and she said, "Well, where they took the menfolk." And then he killed her and she dropped down dead here, just in front of this door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please put the initials SK at the location on the photograph where your daughter's body fell when she was shot.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Mrs. Kaplan, if you could please put your initials and today's date in the white area along the side of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again today's date, please; 16 May, 2006.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, before that photo's removed, I have one other question. Mrs. Kaplan, do you know who shot your daughter Sanida?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, I didn't know at the time, but I learnt who he was later, a month or two later. They told me. The women told me, because he was there. He was the commander there in their hamlet, and they knew him and they told me that it was him. Dragan --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last name. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the person's name, please.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Dragan Unojza [phoen] was the man's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, for the record can you please spell the family name of this person, if you know.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: B-o-n-o-j-z-a [as interpreted], Bunoza. That's the surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kaplan. At the time Dragan Bunoza shot your daughter Sanida, where was he standing?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Do you want me to mark it here? He was here and she was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please put his initials, DB, at the location on the photograph where Dragan Bunoza was standing when he shot your daughter.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Here. Right next to this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how far was Dragan Bunoza when he shot and killed your daughter Sanida?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: One metre away. One metre 10, 1 metre 20. Not further than that. We were all standing round about, close to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I take it, Mrs. Kaplan, in -- earlier when you told the Presiding Judge that you'd testified in a case in Mostar, this was about the killing of your daughter Sanida; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you present in the courtroom when the verdict was announced in the case against Dragan Bunoza?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When was this trial, Mrs. Kaplan, the trial of Dragan Bunoza?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I just can't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate time period? Was it a year ago, five years ago, 10 years ago?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, two years ago. It might have been two years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was the verdict in the court in Mostar in the case against Dragan Bunoza?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They accused him of being a killer, and he was sentenced to nine years' imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The photograph can now be retrieved from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could perhaps move the ELMO again as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, if I could now ask you about what happened to you immediately after your daughter was killed. Can you please tell us what happened immediately after your daughter was shot.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I can tell you this: I stood by my daughter, but then I left, because he kept saying, "Get out." And I left, as I said. I had to turn away from her and join the other people, and I joined the column of people. And as they came across civilians, they would round them up and make them march in front of them. Our people, the civilians were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, who was it that said, "Get out"?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: That killer. He said I should move away from my Sanida. That's what the killer said, "Go," and that I shouldn't keep turning round and trying to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, on this day, 13 July, 1993, was Dragan Bunoza alone?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. There were lots of soldiers. But he came into our house, and he killed her. There were lots of soldiers going up and down the village, making people go in front of them. They would go from house to house and say, "Get out." But he came up to the gate, went into the yard and killed her, the man that killed her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On this day, Mrs. Kaplan, was there any fighting in the village?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, there was no fighting that day there, but they said that there was fighting in Satorova Gomila, that that's where the fighting was. And they made us go that way, to Satorova Gomila, to be a human shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Kaplan, you told us just a few moments ago, page 21, line 6, "As they came across civilians, they would round them up ..." Who were these civilians?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what were the gender and ages of these civilians?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: From two months old to 60 or 65 years old, maybe even older. Women, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where were these people taken? Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We all went together, all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We went -- they took us to the main road, and then they put us in trucks and transferred us to Jasoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how far is it from your village to Jasoc?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: About seven kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what did you do in Jasoc?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Once we got there, they told us, "You won't go up there to Satorova Gomila." This is what I understood from other people, because I wasn't quite myself. This is what I learned later. They said that we should go to school building and that Veselko Raguz had ordered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We went to the school building, and this is where they put us in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in what town or village was this school located?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Aladinici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that a photograph be shown to the witness -- two photographs; 9557 and 9558.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ms. Kaplan, you're now looking at what's been marked P 9557. Do you recognise that, what's depicted in that photo?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that's a photo of?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: This is the school, and this in front is something that remained. But this is the school building. This is where we were incarcerated, in this school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mrs. Kaplan, if you could take that thick red marker, please, and make an X on the school building.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, ma'am, if you could please initial and date that photograph.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if the witness can now be shown P 09558.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, do you recognise what's depicted on the photograph P 09558?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's the school, too, where we were incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please place an X on the building that you recognise as the school where you were incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kaplan. And again, if you could please initial and date that photograph.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Kaplan. Now, do you know if that school had any other names or went by any other names?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The school was called Branko Sotra. That's what they called it. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you tell us how long you were incarcerated in that school?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: For about ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how many people were in that school?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: About 3.000 of us. They were civilians, the elderly, children. All civilians. All civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe what the conditions were like in this school during the 10-day period that you were incarcerated there.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Terrible. There was nothing there. No paper. It was dirty. It was horrible. It was horrible. People all over corridors, sleeping on cement. We had to sleep wherever we could find a spot, on cement. Terrible conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What were the -- you told us they were the elderly and children. Can you give us an approximate range of the ages of the people that were in that school?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: From 65 to 80 years old. Those were the elderly. And then there were young people, too, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How young were the children that you saw there?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: From one month and on. There were children who were one month old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, Mrs. Kaplan, how many rooms were in the school?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I can't remember. Ten, 12 rooms in all. From 10 to 12. I couldn't go out really, I'm sorry, but I heard that's how many there were. Ten to 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the sanitary conditions in the school.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Bad. Really bad. We couldn't go out. And in one room we had to relieve ourselves. We were unable to go out. There was nothing else to do. We had to do it in the rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what type of food or water was available for drinking?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: It was bad. We had no water at all. It was really bad. The water from the well was polluted, but we had to drink it nevertheless. And the food was really bad. It wasn't until the fifth day that they brought us some food, some bread and some cans. One car brought food for 3.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What kind of food did they bring? You said bread and some cans.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Fish cans, and bread; nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How frequently did they bring food?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Once a day while we were there, but we didn't receive anything for four days, and then only on the fifth day we received something. But some people didn't get anything to eat because they ran out of food by the time they got to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, who was bringing this food?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The Croats. They brought it in, the food. It was their truck. All of this was theirs. It all came from their bakery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What -- Mrs. Kaplan, what, if anything, was preventing you and the other people at this school from simply leaving?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, there were soldiers around the school. They were placed there, the guards, and we couldn't go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mrs. Kaplan, for the record, who were these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the reason why you eventually left this school.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: One morning, early, they woke us up. Prior to that, the humanitarian people came in, UNHCR, so they got us up and they took us to two areas, Djulica and another place. They had to separate us because we couldn't all fit in one mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, I neglected to ask you something else about the time you were in the school. Were you kept in the same room or area of that school for the 10-day period you were there?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you've told us, ma'am, that there were about 3.000 people in this school. Where were these people from, do you know?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. This was Stolac municipality and the villages. The people were all from there, rounded up there. I don't know how many villages there are there, but all of them were from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us that the humanitarian people came in, UNHCR. Where did they take you? You personally, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. They got us away. They took us away so that they wouldn't see us there. Many trucks came, and they removed us away because they had learned that they would be passing next to the school and they didn't want them to see us there, imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So who took you away in the trucks?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The HVO. They brought in the trucks, and we were transported in their trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how do you know that the humanitarian people would be passing next to the school?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Once we came home, and once we were there, we saw the UNHCR pass on the road in front of our houses. It was about a kilometre away, but we could still see them, travelling on the road. And this is why they had gotten us away. That was what we gathered, all of us together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And now again, where were you personally taken by the HVO in these trucks? Where did you -- where did they take you to?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They took us back to our houses. To my house, where I used to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how many other people were taken back to your house?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: In our house there were about 250 people. And there are 13 households there. So they put people in those houses. Of course, we couldn't all fit in one house, so they distributed them among these 13 households, 13 houses. And people couldn't all fit there, so some were taken to Djulic, that village or, rather, that hamlet, and lot of people were staying there. That's what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, then, there were 250 people spread among the 13 houses in your hamlet.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's how many there were in my house alone. And in the hamlet there were about 1.000 or more of us. I didn't go out, so I can't tell you exactly how many people there were there, but I know that in our house alone there were 250 people. I didn't get out, so I couldn't tell you whether in other houses there were 50 people or more, but definitely there were more than 1.000 altogether in the hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How were you able to accommodate this many people in your house?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We had an older house and a newer house, and then one house that hadn't been completed. So people were everywhere; in the yard, in these houses. One couldn't really step for fear of -- step anywhere for fear on trampling on people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where were these people sleeping?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Inside, outside, everywhere. Wherever they found a spot. In the yard, in corridors, in rooms. Everywhere. Because when you are a refugee, you have to find accommodation. They slept in the garage; everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Mrs. Kaplan, what were the gender and ages of the people who were -- who were accommodated in your house?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were two or three elderly persons in our house, and then others were in other houses. We had three or four people who were between 70 and 80 years old. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, how did you feed all of these people?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, we had some food in our house, and then the HVO would come, and they would go to other villages to pick what was left there and they would bring it to people so they could cook and prepare it. They would take women and children to a hamlet to get flour, oil, whatever was there. And then people would also bring in their food from their mahalas. And then, you know, they would come in trucks and say, "Well, who is going to come with us to go get some food?" So it was mostly the children, the young people, who went with the HVO to get food. You know, they would say, "Come on, you children -" 13- and 14-year-olds - "you're stronger than women, so come with us to get some food."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, these people that were accommodated in your house, were they free to leave?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. No. The HVO would come to get them. They had orders. Nobody could leave. We had guards all around us. We were only allowed to leave if they asked you to go in their truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall, Mrs. Kaplan, the approximate date that you returned to your house?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: You mean after the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No. When you were taken from the school back to your house.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: When we were all crammed in. Well, the 22nd, 23rd of July, around those dates, because we stayed there for some ten days. Around that time. I'm not sure. 22nd, 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, the year, Mrs. Kaplan?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, how long -- approximately how long did all of these people remain crammed in, as you put it, crammed in your house?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, we came, let's say, on the 22nd or 23rd, and we left on the 2nd of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us the circumstances under which you left on the 2nd of August, 1993? What happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Early in the morning, people - children, women - were getting up, and we saw the buses on the road - buses, trucks. And then they said you're going to Djulici and we're going to put you on trucks there. And that's what it was; they got everybody up, marching in columns, going there. They searched us there and then they took us to a house in twos and threes, and they searched all of us. They would take three people in and then search us, and then later on you would join the column, and we were put on buses and went to the Buna. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At this point in time, Mrs. Kaplan, the 2nd of August, 1993, where was the rest of your family?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: In camps. My husband was in a camp. I also had a minor son, and he was taken the day before we were taken, to Buna. They took him on the 1st and us on the 2nd. They took us to Buna. As I said to you, he was my minor son. And then I had another son, and all of them were in prison, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us, ma'am, that on the 2nd of August you were taken to Buna. How many people were taken with you to Buna on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Only the elderly. Whoever couldn't go to Dretelj. Just the elderly over 70 years old, and whoever was below 70 was taken to prison from that place once we were expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How many people, approximately, were with you in Buna on or about the 2nd of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't all go together. I'm not sure. In our mahala, there were maybe up to 30, and in the other place, in other mahala, I don't know. I can't remember. And I don't know whether they went before or after. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, again for our record, can you tell the Trial Chamber what a mahala is.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Mahala is a village. We refer to a village as mahala, or to a hamlet we refer to mahala, where a group of people lives. Sometimes we say mahala, sometimes we say hamlet, but that means the same thing. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that clarification. Now, where did you go from Buna?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We went to Blagaj. We walked for five or six kilometres, and then our army met us there, the army, and they loaded us on trucks and they took us to Blagaj. There was just one vehicle, and it took them all the way up to late hours of that evening to transport all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the conditions were like as you walked this five or six kilometres from Buna to Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They fired but over our heads. They didn't fire at us. They fired, but we didn't get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What personal property did you take with you when you left your home on that day as you were being transported to Buna?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We took a blanket and just maybe a few things, but mostly they made us throw things away. We had perhaps some plastic bags and another bag, and we could take some clothes with us, and the rest was thrown away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. I am just about finished with the direct examination, but I would ask if we take the recess now. I'll review my notes, but it should only be a question of 10 to 15 minutes at the max, and perhaps much less than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. It is just about 10.30. We will have a 20-minute break and we will reconvene at 10 minutes to eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, I just have a few questions left for you. You told us earlier today that your husband, Hamza Kaplan, was taken to a camp. Can you tell us where he was taken to and how long he was there?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: He was taken to Dretelj, and he stayed there for about two months, or one month -- well, let's say two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did your husband describe for you how he was treated in Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, they didn't beat him much, just twice, about twice. But he was in Dretelj. They did beat him a bit, but not too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe his physical appearance when you first saw him after his release from Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, he looked very poorly when he was released from Dretelj. We couldn't recognise him. I as his wife couldn't recognise him when he came back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know during the time he was in Dretelj if anyone went to visit him or take him anything?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. One day my sister-in-law tried. Five or six women from the mahala, from our mahala, from our hamlet went, but I think they only got as far as the gate, and they didn't let them -- took the food away from them, the food that they were bringing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, about what your son Samir Kaplan? What prison was he taken to and for how long?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: He was taken to Dretelj, and he stayed there a long time; nine months. He was one of the last to leave. Until the very last person left the camp. He was at Dretelj, then Heliodrom, but he survived. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And your son Ibrahim Kaplan, where was he detained?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: He was detained for one day and one night, and then he was taken to Dretelj. He was a minor, underage, and then he was released when his father was released. They were quite -- he was a minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How old was he at the time he was taken away and detained?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Fifteen years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you told us he was detained for one day and one night, and then he was taken to Dretelj. Where was he detained for one day and one night?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. In Stolac. It's called the police station, Kostana. And then he was taken to several places, but he just spent the night in Stolac at the police station, and then they took him to Kostana, and from Kostana there were other prisoners, too, and they were all taken to Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, ma'am, what is Kostana?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: It's a hospital for bone -- for fractures, and we called it the bone hospital, Kostana. For fractures. Orthopaedic hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in what town is Kostana hospital located?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: In Stolac. In Stolac proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, at the time your husband Hamza Kaplan and your son Ibrahim Kaplan were released, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They went to the hills above Jablanica. They were released there, then they went to Jablanica and on foot to Blagaj, where we were put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, how far is it from Jablanica to Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly. Quite a long way away. I can't really say how many kilometres, but quite far. I can't really give you an estimate. Perhaps you know this better than I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you -- do you recall, Mrs. Kaplan, how long it took your husband Hamza Kaplan and your son Ibrahim Kaplan to walk from Jablanica to Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Four days and four nights. They walked. They went on foot. They didn't dare walk during the day, so they walked at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you tell us about your brother-in-law Salko Kaplan. Where was he taken to?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I'll explain you -- I'll explain that to you. On the 1st of August he was taken out of our house to Stolac. The police or the soldiers took him away. And he was there, Mirko was there -- Mirko Raguz, and Mirko Pazin [phoen]. They came by and asked us where he was. And we said that some soldiers had come by and taken him off. And he told us -- they told us they would go and get him. But they sent him back the same day. He spent the night there. And then when we were expelled, he was taken to prison, to Stolac, and then further on to Dretelj. So that's quite clear how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what happened to your brother-in-law Salko Kaplan while he was detained?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: In Stolac, my Ibrahim, he was with him at the Kostana hospital. They beat him up there. And then he went to Dretelj. He lived for 10 days, but then he succumbed to his wounds and died.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, "he lived for 10 days and then he succumbed," who are you referring to? Who is the "he"?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: That's right, yes. How do you mean? That's the Salko, the Salko they killed. And then he succumbed to the injuries. Well, those soldiers beat him in Stolac. I don't know exactly who.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, Mrs. Kaplan, what happened to the body of Salko Kaplan?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: When he died, they buried him at Muminovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My final series of questions, ma'am, concerns your daughter Sanida. Were you present at her funeral? Were you present at her funeral?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. No. No. How could I when I was held prisoner in the schoolhouse? The only people who attended was my son, he was at home at the time, and there were six or eight civilians who were not captured in that first round. And when they learnt that she had been killed, they came out and said, "We'll bury her." And at that point the army turned up, the soldiers turned up. They surrendered, and they were taken to Harem, and they buried her, my son and seven other people with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how is it that your son and these others had not been captured during that first round, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: They didn't go to any shelter, no. They just hid. And then they buried her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, were you ever issued or did you ever request a death certificate with respect to your daughter Sanida?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. When I went to Blagaj. I got a certificate saying she was dead and that she is no longer living. We had to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, ma'am, when you were interviewed by the Tribunal, you provided a copy of that death certificate to the investigator; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the registry, we'd like to show the witness P 08789, which is in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, can you see a document in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: This one here, you mean, or this one over here? Yes, I can see it says Kaplan, Sanida, born on the 24th of July, 1950, in Stolac municipality, Stolac. Father's name Kaplan Hamza and mother's name Kaplan Fatima, killed on the 13th of July, 1993, in Pjesivac, buried at Pjesivac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And is this the death certificate that you were issued concerning the death of your daughter Sanida Kaplan?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And my final question for you, Mrs. Kaplan: With respect to the court proceedings -- with respect to the court proceedings against Dragan Bunoza, was an exhumation carried out of your daughter's remains?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. They ordered that to be done, and it was done so that they could establish what happened and how it happened. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall what their conclusions were, based on the autopsy that was done?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Of the exhumation, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: As I've already explained, that's how it was. Everything was okay, just like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if you were ever informed what the cause of death was?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: That she was killed, shot in the head and in the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kaplan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm now going to turn towards to the Defence teams for the cross-examination. I'm sure that you've reached some agreement. Have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Kaplan. My name is Tomislav Jonjic, and I will be asking you just a few questions on behalf of the fifth accused.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: I know that in all these events -- with all these events it's very difficult for you to speak, and I express my condolences to you.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: But I'd just like to clarify two or three points.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Today, when you were asked by the Prosecutor, you confirmed that the soldiers who were in your village were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Camouflage uniforms. That's the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether it is true and correct that they had no insignia?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Maybe they did, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the Prosecution, to the investigators, five years ago, you expressly stated that as far as you remember, none of them had any white belts, wore any white belts.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, two or three brief questions. What you've said about Dretelj, you only know that on the basis of what other people told you?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Well, my sons were there, my husband was there, so they knew what happened. They knew how it was in Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You also said that your brother-in-law Salko died as a result of the abuse at the Kostana hospital.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite true.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And one final question: You said that he was buried at Muminovaca. Is Muminovaca a Muslim cemetery?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, Mr. President, for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My name is Bozidar Kovacic, I am Defence counsel for the accused General Slobodan Praljak.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to have to ask you these questions.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Go ahead, ask me. If I can answer, I will; if I can't, I won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, I should like the usher's assistance to place Prosecution Exhibit R65 ter number 090550 -- 09550. In the meantime, I'm going to ask you a question. Mrs. Kaplan, you told us today about the tragic situation when your daughter was killed and you told us that you know that afterwards there were court proceedings that took place and that this man Bunoza was convicted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the transcript, for the record. You also said that you were a witness during that court trial.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kaplan, I'm going to show you the verdict, the judgement, the first page of the Mostar judgement, but before that let me ask you this: Do you remember the president of the Trial Chamber in those court proceedings, who was that?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: I don't know. He didn't introduce himself, but I know that I went to court, but I don't know. Why should I say that I do when I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, take a look at the judgement and then we'll see the name and you'll just help me out and say whether you think, judging on the basis of his name, that he was a Muslim or Croat.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We were all together there, Muslims and Croats, during the trial, but I really don't know who the people were individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. We'll get to that. In the meantime, until we see the document, on the 13th of July, 1993, when they collected you up and when, unfortunately, your daughter was killed, you said that there were a lot of soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were there other cases when people were shot?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Not then, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So that was the only case?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. On that day. What happened later, I can't talk about that, but not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Unfortunately, we don't seem to have the judgement on our screens yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we should put it on the ELMO because obviously there is some problem. We would like the usher to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kaplan, I'm going to ask you for your assistance here. That's the judgement when Bunoza was tried, when you were a witness. First of all, it says, "In the name of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina," then we have an introductory paragraph in which it says the cantonal court in Mostar, with a Trial Chamber composed of Judge Kebo Hamo. Now, I would like to ask you: Kebo Hamo, is that a Muslim name?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, it's a Muslim name, yes, that's it, a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: He was the presiding judge, then we have Pavlovic Slavko and Hasanbegovic Vesna as members of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: One was a Croat and the second name was a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So that's what you said. You said it was a mixed Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask the usher to pick up the document. We don't need it any more. At the end, I would like to tender this document into evidence. Mrs. Kaplan, did you perhaps during that trial and the discussions about this man Bunoza, did you perhaps happen to hear a piece of information to this effect: That another man called Bunoza, who allegedly is Dragan Bonojza's brother -- is that it or is this the Bunoza?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, that's the man. I didn't hear anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that another Bunoza, another man Bunoza was tried for the killing of three HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. I can't tell you about something I didn't know about or didn't hear about, I really don't know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, I'm just asking you. I just thought perhaps you had.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And just one point: Mrs. Kaplan, in view of the village you lived in in the course of 1992, that is to say before the conflict between the Muslims and Croats, most of the population from that area were Serbs or, rather, the Yugoslav People's Army were Serbs and they expelled the people.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. Only when the HVO came, they expelled us. The Serbs did not.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No. The Serbs didn't do anything to us, they didn't touch us, the Serbs, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So in 1992 --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: We were down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: For the record, we have to make pauses between question and answer, but if I understood you correctly, in the course of 1992 while the Serbs and the JNA were on the plateau, they did not expel you.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, they did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Kovacic, would you slow down, please for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... trying to correct this error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But since you are from that area, do you know people from the neighbouring hamlets, the villages in the vicinity of Stolac, were they expelled by the JNA in 1992, from that area?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Those towards that area were expelled by Serbs, and the ones near Stolac and Dubrava were expelled by Croats, but the Serbs expelled the people towards Ljubinje.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were up there were Bosniaks, and then later on we were expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In 1992, when the Serbs expelled Bosniaks, do you know where those Bosniaks went?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Some went to Montenegro. Some went to the Dubrava plateau if they had some relatives there, and some went to Montenegro and elsewhere, towards that area. Some did, and some didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please. Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know in 1992, in the summer, when the HVO regained control over that area, when they had expelled Serbs, the people who had left the villages, did they come back to their villages?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: They didn't?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Some of them who were in Mostar, did they go back to their homes?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, no, they didn't. They went up in the hills, and they didn't dare come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you, madam. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be tendered into evidence, please, as Defence Exhibit under number 3D 00149. [In English] The record on the transcript is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will address later on the question of the tendering of the exhibits. Next Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of General Petkovic has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a little time. Any additional questions or re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: None from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Questions from the Bench. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you first, Mrs. Kaplan, you said that you had 250 people in your house. How do you know it was 250? Did you count them?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: No, I didn't count them. The others did. My brother-in-law counted them and said that's how many there were. I didn't. I was in shock. I was mostly lying down. That's what I heard, that this is how many there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would like to know whether there is any further information or documents on the death of your brother-in-law. Was an autopsy made in that case? Did anybody start the prosecution? Was there any investigation? Could you tell us more about that, please.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
