utterances.text: There was an investigation. His wife went to court, and that's what they said. Nothing's ready yet. The man who beat him has not yet been tried. That's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Hvala.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mrs. Kaplan, I have just one simple question to put to you.

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Please go ahead. I'll tell you whatever I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A while ago the Defence mentioned a judgement which was rendered in Mostar by the cantonal court in a case which prosecuted Dragan Bunoza. Did you attend the trial? Were you present in the courtroom like you are present in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The accused, Dragan Bunoza, was he also there in the courtroom on the day of the trial?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, he was. I saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you are telling us that you have seen him. Did you recognise him as being the man who had killed your daughter?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I looked him in the eye, and I said, "You are the one." He had no questions for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mrs. Kaplan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the witness the following question: You said that one of your sons at the beginning the war had served in the HVO forces. He was wounded also. My question runs as follows: Where was he at the time your daughter was killed and where you yourself were expelled from your village? That's my first question. My second question -- my second question runs as follows: You said your daughter was buried by one of your sons and this other person from your village who had gone into hiding --

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, a relative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military who entered the village, did they know about this, and how did they react to the presence of these people that had gone into hiding in the village?

utterances.speaker: FATA KAPLAN
utterances.text: The situation was very difficult. I told you that they were persecuted, tied up. They did all kinds of things to them. However, they survived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If there are no further questions, Mrs. Kaplan, the Trial Chamber would like to thank you for having come to The Hague. On behalf of the Bench, I wish you well, and I wish you a safe return. I would like to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you all. Everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall now give the floor to Mr. Mundis so that he can tender his exhibits into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We would ask that the following documents and photographs be admitted into evidence: P 08789, which was the death certificate of Sanida Kaplan. P 09067, the photograph of Sanida Kaplan. P 09555, a photograph of the house where Sanida Kaplan was killed. P 9 -- excuse me. P 09556, a photograph of the house where Sanida Kaplan was killed. P 09557, a photograph of the school where Mrs. Kaplan was detained. P 09558, a second photograph of the school where Mrs. Kaplan was detained. I guess those need IC numbers for the ones that were marked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Registrar, there are those exhibits that were marked for identification in addition to documents that have been annotated by the witness, which will have an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The following exhibits are therefore admitted: P 08789, P 09067. The four pictures, photos marked by the hand of the witness shall be given the following IC numbers: IC 0008, which was marked on the original picture 09 -- P 09555. IC 0009 -- sorry, IC 00009, marked by the witness on the original P 09556. IC 00010, marked on the original P 09557. IC 00011, marked on the original P 09558. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Mr. Kovacic, are you asking for the judgement of the cantonal court of Mostar to be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would -- I would ask to admit the judgement to the evidence, and it should be recorded under number 3D 00149.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kovacic. Registrar. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit is therefore tendered and admitted under the reference 3D 00149, with a specific mention that the original document -- or it's based on the original document P 09550. So we'll have two references for the same document. This is for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we've now settled the question of the documents. We still have a little time left. I would like to inform the people present of the courtroom of the following: We had been seized by an oral motion pertaining to the fact that the accused should gain access to a portable computer. As things stand, we have discussed this, and I am expecting a response to a memo I have sent to the Registry. As soon as I get a response from the Registry, we will let you know what decision will be taken. The second motion that was filed by the Defence is still pending. This pertains to the fact that the accused should be sitting next to their lawyer. I have also sent a memo to the Registry regarding this particular issue, and I have had no answer in writing as yet. As soon as the Registry responds, we will render our decision. In addition, I've been informed about the fact that at the beginning of the morning that the Defence team had filed a motion with a view to certifying an appeal after the decision on time allocated to the Defence was rendered for the cross-examination. We have not yet had enough time to look into this motion. We will, of course, render a decision to -- on this request for certification of -- the Prosecution can also state its point of view regarding this particular matter. Mr. Mundis, I don't know whether you intend to give us your view on the merits of the motion filed by the Defence. I shall now give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps Mr. Scott and I ask discuss this after court and inform the Chamber's legal officer whether we will be filing something, and if so, when. I wouldn't imagine that our response, if we choose to go down that path, would be one that would take us a significant period of time to prepare, but if we could, we would ask for that, that we simply contact the Chamber's legal officer later this afternoon, indicating if we will file a response, and if so, when, but we would certainly be doing that in the remainder of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If you intend to file any submissions, please do so quickly, because we need to have all the available information if we are to render a decision. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just take a few moments, there's one other issue I would ask to raise at this point in time, and I would like to do that in closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back into open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in open session, would anybody like to address a particular issue? I'm turning to the Prosecution. Nothing which you would like to address? Let me turn to the Defence counsel. Nobody wishes to address any particular issue. In that case, I would like to address the question of the schedule with the Prosecution, the schedule for next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have three witnesses scheduled for next. The calendar has been previously provided. In the event any of those witnesses seek protective measures, I'm not going to mention the names, but the three witnesses who appear on the schedule that was provided, I guess it was late last week, will be appearing commencing Monday afternoon at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We need to look a little bit into the future. The Bench have discussed this matter, and after the summer recess, we shall resume our hearing on Monday the 14th of August, at a quarter past two. So I'm just giving you this date so that you can make your own arrangements. Our last week of hearing in July may be reduced by one day because the Judges attend the Plenary Session. As you know, it is in July that the Judges meet to amend the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and at that time there is one hearing that cannot take place because of the Plenary Session. As a general rule, there is no hearing on that day, but I will advise you of the schedule which is set by the President of this Tribunal so that you can make your own arrangements. The Plenary may well take place on the Thursday, in which case we would -- we would be sitting on the Monday, the Tuesday, and the Wednesday, and there would be no hearing on the Thursday and not on the Friday either. But we shall see when the time comes. I want to make sure that you can make your own arrangements. The hearing for tomorrow and Thursday has been cancelled because one of the witnesses which was called -- who was called to testify cannot come. This is a Prosecution witness. This same situation may occur again. There's nothing we can do about it. And when the Defence counsel will call their witnesses to come and testify, the Defence counsel may encounter the same kind of problem. This is something we just need to face up to. Nobody is responsible for this. It's a judicial process which is responsible for this kind of problem. Sometimes the witnesses cannot attend at a time we would like them to attend, but rest assured we do all we can to make sure that the witnesses attend or are called to testify when they should. If there is no other issue to be addressed, I would like you to attend our next hearing, which will be next Monday at a quarter past two. I will have the pleasure of seeing you again next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of May, 2006, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
